title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 6
preview: Brad took the biggest beating of the season, Maddox's Unbreakable Vow got re-bound, the Commish let three running backs rot on his bench, and overtime murdered the median. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Wow, that just happened. What's next? Week 5 gave us a 70.7-point blowout, three overtime games that wrecked the median, and a commissioner who benched fifty points of running backs. Week 6 kicks off Thursday. Nobody is safe.
facts_note: Every fact is real Sleeper data: Week 5 results and lineups, transactions through Wednesday Oct 14 at 5 PM ET (including the overnight waiver run and the day's free-agent and commissioner moves), injuries, and Week 6 matchups. "Projected" = Sleeper Week 6 projections in league scoring for lineups as set Wednesday around 5:30 PM ET (lineups can change). A roast among friends.

entries.roast: Fifty points. FIFTY. Braelon Allen 20.6, Blake Corum 16.2, Emanuel Wilson 13.2, all sitting on the Commish's bench while he lost by 4.75. Meanwhile Jeremiyah Love is in the lineup scoring 2.2 like a man on a union break. Braelon, you let the whole team down. Blake, you let the whole team down. Emanuel, you let the whole team down. Nobody let anybody down! There's one guy in this building with a pencil, and he's wearing the crown. You wrote the rulebook, you hold the clipboard, and you still managed to get robbed by yourself. Supreme Leader? Supreme Leader of the bench, baby.
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano. Projected 151.6 to 145.6. Braelon Allen (11.4) is on the bench again, behind Jeremiyah Love (10.1).
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 6, and Braelon Allen scores 15 on the bench, because of course he does.

entries.roast: You ever notice the guy getting blown out by 70.7 is always the one who calls it early? Brad conceded while the games were still going, like walking out of a movie before the bus hits him. Josh Allen gave him 35.1 and he still lost by 70.7, which takes real talent, because RJ Harvey gave him 0.7 and CeeDee Lamb gave him 2.9. Why do they call it a skill position if nobody's showing any? Brad has given up 941.5 points in five weeks. At this point he isn't playing a fantasy team, he's hosting one. Everybody's best week gets its own guest room.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet. Projected 144.0 to 133.1. Mahomes is back next to Josh Allen, and the new kicker (Nick Folk, off waivers) and new defense (Chiefs, added at 6:01 this morning) cover the Detroit and Cincinnati byes.
entries.prediction: Brad wins by 11 and still gives up 130, which for him counts as a rest day.

entries.roast: Maddox scored 218.2, the best week in the league, and left 100.9 points on his bench. Think about that. The man won the lottery and mailed half the check to the wrong address. And what do we do with a guy like that? We hand him Shedeur Sanders. He cut Shedeur like a bad tattoo, and the Commish keeps sewing him back on. In Harry Potter, you break one and you die. In this league, you break one and it just keeps showing up on your roster. And I think that's worse. Now he's starting a Vikings defense that's on bye. Even the universe is saying, hey, just stop.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo. Projected 124.0 to 111.0. Maddox is starting the Vikings defense, the same Vikings D he offered up in the Shedeur ransom, and Minnesota is on bye. That's a zero in the lineup until he fixes it. Bucky Irving is questionable, and Shedeur is on the bench, where the vow can keep an eye on him.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins anyway, cuts Shedeur by Friday, and Shedeur is back by Saturday.

entries.roast: Brian is 7-3, second in the league, and his kicker Cairo Santos scored a zero. Zero. I don't know how that happens. I think he went in for a field goal and the ball filed a complaint. Jaylen Warren scored 39.8 and dragged that team across the line like a dad carrying a drunk uncle out of a wedding. Somewhere tonight there's a masked figure on a rooftop, fighting in the shadows for a city that doesn't know his name. Turns out he's just Brian, and he got lucky. Anyway, 7-3. Good for him.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Kasik. Projected 142.8 to 151.6. Bryce Young starts with Deshaun Watson at superflex, and Caleb Williams (doubtful) stays on the bench.
entries.prediction: Brian loses by 8 and nobody hears about it until Tuesday.

entries.roast: I'm telling ya, Kasik lost by 4.0 and he's a lawyer. A lawyer! He can't win an argument with his own bench. Justin Herbert started for 6.95 while Daniel Jones sat there with 13.75. I tell ya, I get no respect. Neither does Daniel Jones. The guy's been sitting there for weeks like a coat at a bad party. And the kicker, Matt Gay, gave him 5.0. My wife says I kick like that. Look, I'm a lawyer. I object to everything. Overruled. Sustained. Whatever. I lost by four, and I had the evidence in my pocket the whole time. I need a drink.
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill. Projected 151.6 to 142.8. Zay Flowers and Nico Collins are both questionable starters, and Daniel Jones finally starts at QB next to Herbert.
entries.prediction: Kasik wins by 9 and bills Brian for the hours.

entries.roast: Mike benched T.J. Hockenson for 26.9, so the next week he did the smart thing and started him for 1.7. Hockenson is the ex who waits until you've moved on, then shows up in a parked car outside. Mike keeps taking him back, and every time he gets the same text: I've changed. He hasn't, Mike! He went 1.7! Mike also survived Sunday's overtime against Kasik, then lost the median by less than a point anyway, so the overtime survived him and still sent a bill. Travis Kelce scored a zero on a bye, the only guy on that roster who knew exactly what he was doing.
entries.this_week: vs Brad Kochheiser. Projected 133.1 to 144.0. Lamar Jackson (questionable, 21.4 projected) sits for Jameis Winston (13.1), Kelce is back at tight end with Hockenson on bye, and Mike Evans and DeVonta Smith are questionable starters.
entries.prediction: Mike loses by 7, and Lamar's points on the bench get entered into evidence.

entries.roast: So I'm gonna tell you about Kyle, because Kyle is not okay. Man loses by 8.15, scores the lowest total in the league, and has D'Andre Swift sitting on his bench for 17.3. I said Swift, Kyle! SWIFT! You had him right there! And Romeo Doubs is in the lineup with 2.6, a man out here playing like he owes somebody money. Then Kyle finds out a fumble costs a point and sits there like a man with a calculator crying. He needed nine reversed fumbles to win. Nine! Mm-mm. You don't need a referee, Kyle. You need a priest.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer. Projected 145.6 to 151.6. Goff and St. Brown are on the Lions' bye, so Stafford and Sam Darnold run the quarterback spots.
entries.prediction: Kyle loses by 6 and files a formal complaint about the fumble rule. Denied.

entries.roast: Okay, listen. Drew wins 212.55 to 145.45. Everybody's happy, right? Wrong. Because this is the same man who offered Jayden Daniels and Sam LaPorta to Cardillo, and then Drew started them against him anyway. 53.55 points. You tried to sell the guy the gun, and then you shot him with it! Man pawned your car and then used it for the getaway. And now he's 4-6 and posting watch out with a smirk emoji like he's the Godfather. Brother, you're not the Godfather. You're the guy who brings the cannoli.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado. Projected 138.8 to 136.6. Jayden Daniels, Puka Nacua and Jalen Coker are all questionable in the starting lineup, with Geno Smith (13.6) waiting on the bench.
entries.prediction: Drew wins by 3 and posts "watch out" again, unprompted.

entries.roast: Taylor beat the Commish by 4.75, and I want everybody to know how little that proves, because Cam Skattebo gave him 6.1 and the Commanders defense gave him 5.1. So what did he do? Fired the defense. AGAIN. The Colts are number eight. EIGHT! Taylor doesn't own a defense, he runs a hostel for them. Then the tight ends: Tyler Higbee, Kyle Pitts, Dallas Goedert and Darren Waller. He's collecting tight ends like Pokemon cards and he still started the doubtful one. Sad!
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman. Projected 136.6 to 138.8. Dallas Goedert (doubtful) is the starting tight end while Kyle Pitts, Darren Waller and Tyler Higbee sit, and the brand-new Colts defense gets its first start.
entries.prediction: Taylor loses by 2, blames the defense, and defense number nine shows up by Friday.

entries.roast: Cardillo, my man. Drake Maye scored 45.2 for him, the highest single score in the league. George Pickens scored 30.0. And Cardillo still lost by 67.1! How?! The man had a monster week and got hit by a bus. Then the median beat him by 1.18, because three games went to overtime and not one of his players was in any of them. Not one! His guys were all in the car by the second quarter, like it was a Costco run. Rookie mistake. Draft players who play in overtime.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox. Projected 111.0 to 124.0, the lowest set lineup in the league. Carnell Tate (14.0) sits behind Luther Burden (12.3) at flex, the running backs are Kyle Monangai (4.6) and Roschon Johnson (4.3), and Maddox is starting a Vikings defense that's on bye.
entries.prediction: Cardillo loses by 9, and every game in the league goes to overtime except his.
